item.research_question: How does stacking fault (SF) strengthening contribute to work hardening behavior during deformation in a low stacking fault energy (SFE) high entropy alloy, and how does it co-activate with transformation-induced plasticity (TRIP) to overcome the strength-ductility tradeoff?
item.material_system: Fe40Mn20Cr15Co20Si5 (at%) high entropy alloy with SFE ~ 6.31 mJ m−2
item.processing_route: Vacuum induction casting to produce as-cast (AC) condition; subsequent friction stir processing (FSP) with a tungsten-rhenium tool (shoulder diameter 12 mm, pin length 3.5 mm) at 350 RPM and 50.8 mm/min traverse speed to produce AC + FSP condition
item.test_conditions: In-situ tensile deformation on the VULCAN neutron diffractometer at the Spallation Neutron Source (SNS) using bulk specimens with a gauge volume of ~135 mm3
key_findings: The stacking fault interspacing (LSF) decreased from an initial state to ~50 nm in the AC condition and ~10 nm in the AC + FSP condition during tensile deformation.
SF strengthening contributions (σSF) were quantified as ~50 MPa for the AC condition and ~250 MPa for the AC + FSP condition.
A sustained work hardening rate (θ) of around ~3000 MPa was observed in the AC + FSP condition, whereas the AC condition exhibited a more rapid decrease.
The decrease in LSF slowed and reached a plateau coinciding with the onset of the γ-f.c.c. → ε-h.c.p. transformation.
The AC + FSP condition showed a delayed decrease in LSF compared to the AC condition, attributed to the high density of faults formed during FSP.
The final saturated LSF of ~10 nm in the AC + FSP condition was similar to values observed in Mg alloys (~16 nm) and Co alloys (~10 nm).
The cooperative activation of SF strengthening and TRIP was evidenced by the simultaneous increase in σSF and the intensity of the ε-h.c.p. {10.1} peak.
item.mechanism: Stacking faults act as barriers to dislocation motion, increasing strength as their interspacing (LSF) decreases. The onset of γ-f.c.c. → ε-h.c.p. transformation relieves stress concentrations caused by dislocation pile-ups, which explains the plateau in LSF decrease. The simultaneous activation of SF strengthening and TRIP allows for sustained work hardening and overcomes the conventional strength-ductility compromise.
item.limitations: The text notes that discrepancies in measured Si and Mn content by Atom Probe Tomography (APT) are due to field ion evaporation effects, and that the study does not draw definitive conclusions regarding comparisons of TRIP HEAs with TRIP steels due to the need for additional research.
item.future_work: The authors state that the question of whether SFs contributed to strengthening in TRIP steels while the transformed fraction decreased with increasing strength requires additional research to draw conclusions.
quotes: Cooperative activation of multiple mechanisms was indicated by increases in SF strengthening and γ-f.c.c. → ε-h.c.p. transformation leading to a simultaneous increase in strength and ductility.
The decrease in LSF slowed, marked by a change in slope approaching plastic deformation.
The stress relief with activation of transformation can explain the plateau in SF interspacing observed in the present study.
